content.thinking:
I need to verify that the recent documentation edits and the FP4‑related changes haven’t broken the full training pipeline. Earlier I launched the end‑to‑end test `tests/e2e/test_train_entry.py` and observed it taking about 15 minutes, likely because sparse attention is slower than dense. I even set up a background wait for that process (PID 2650949) so I could continue working while it runs.

While waiting, I profiled the model speed for sparse vs. dense (and with FP4) and got concrete numbers (≈25 ms/step for sparse, ≈37 ms/step for sparse + FP4). Those results look reasonable, but they don’t confirm that the entire training script still runs to completion after the doc updates and the new `linear_type` logic.

The safest way to check the pipeline now is to invoke a focused end‑to‑end test that runs the full training loop but with prints enabled so I can see any errors or warnings. I’ll use the specific test `test_full_pipeline_end_to_end` inside `tests/e2e/test_train_entry.py`. To keep the session responsive, I should run it with a timeout—four minutes (240 s) should be ample given the earlier ~15 min run was due to the full suite; this single test should finish much quicker. I’ll also add `-s` to allow stdout prints and `-q` for minimal pytest noise.

The test output includes progress bars that contain `%` characters; those clutter the tail view. I’ll pipe the output through `grep -v "%|"` to strip any lines containing a percent sign or a pipe (the typical progress‑bar characters). Finally, I only need the most recent information, so I’ll pipe to `tail -30` to show the last 30 lines.

Because I still have the original e2e test running in the background, I don’t want this new command to block the session. I’ll run it in the background as well, using the `run_in_background` flag, and give it a generous overall timeout (250 000 ms) to ensure the command itself is killed if it hangs. This will let me continue monitoring other tasks while the test executes.

All of this translates to a Bash tool call that runs:

```bash
timeout 240 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_train_entry.py::test_full_pipeline_end_to_end -q -s 2>&1 \
    | grep -v "%|\" \
    | tail -30
```

with `run_in_background: true`. This should give me a concise, filtered view of the end‑to‑end pipeline execution without stalling the session.
